title: Vicky Kaushal Has Disappeared — to Become a God
excerpt: Eighteen months. One role. Zero distractions. Inside Mahavatar, Bollywood's most extreme actor commitment in years — and the ₹300 crore gamble Ranveer Singh is making right beside him.
body:
Somewhere in Mumbai, **Vicky Kaushal** is waking up at dawn, eating clean, lifting heavy, and not returning calls from filmmakers. The man who made the nation weep in *Sardar Udham* and had it roaring through *Chhaava* has gone deliberately quiet — and if everything goes to plan, you won't see him in anything new for a year and a half.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=2xgITictQXY</youtube>

The reason is **Mahavatar**.

Directed by **Amar Kaushik** — the man behind *Stree* and *Bhediya* — and produced by **Maddock Films**, *Mahavatar* is a mythological epic centred on **Chiranjeevi Parashurama**, the sixth avatar of Vishnu and one of the seven immortals of Hindu legend. A warrior-sage who wields an axe of divine origin, Parashurama is revered as the eternal defender of dharma — fierce, unrelenting, and ageless. Kaushal is building his body to match.

The first look, unveiled on Parashuram Jayanti back in November 2024, was a statement of intent: long matted hair, an intense stare, and a weapon in hand. But the real commitment has unfolded behind the scenes. Since June 2026, Kaushal has been deep in a six-month preparation phase — physical transformation, character workshops, total immersion — designed to turn the lean, athletic frame he carried through **Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War** into a wrestler-like build befitting an immortal warrior.

> "The actor cannot begin his physical prep as he is currently shooting Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love & War, in which he sports an athletic look." — Mid-Day

With *Love and War* now behind him, the distractions are gone. Filming on *Mahavatar* is scheduled to begin in January 2027 and will consume the rest of the year. Kaushal has committed to taking zero other films during this period — a rarity in an industry where top actors routinely juggle three or four productions simultaneously. The decision echoes **Aamir Khan's** famous single-film years but stretches even further: eighteen months of total immersion for one role, from prep to final shot.

Originally slated for a Christmas 2026 theatrical release, *Mahavatar* has been pushed to 2027 — reports suggest an Independence Day weekend bow — as Bhansali's demanding production schedule rippled into Maddock's timeline. Nobody at the production house seems troubled. The extra months mean more time for the VFX-heavy post-production that a project of this scale demands, and more time for Kaushal to fully inhabit a character whose mythology spans millennia.

The film is Maddock's most ambitious production to date, and the studio's horror-universe track record — over ₹1,000 crore from *Stree*, *Bhediya*, and *Munjya* — proves they know how to deliver spectacle with personality.

**And Vicky isn't alone in going big.**

Just as Kaushal seals himself away, **Ranveer Singh** is gearing up for **Pralay**, a ₹300 crore post-apocalyptic survival thriller directed by **Jai Mehta**. Shooting is scheduled to begin this August, with AI-driven visuals and physical sets merging to create a dystopian world unlike anything attempted in Hindi cinema. South Indian star **Kalyani Priyadarshan** has been confirmed opposite Singh, marking her Hindi debut — a fresh pairing that nobody saw coming.

Singh, who has reportedly moved on from the *Don* franchise, is pivoting toward uncharted genre territory. Kaushal is going deeper into myth than any mainstream Bollywood star in years. Together, they signal something important happening at the top of the industry: fewer films, longer prep, bigger swings.

For NRI audiences — many of whom made *Chhaava* a diaspora hit and turned *Dhurandhar* into a global phenomenon — both projects are worth watching closely. *Mahavatar* is being positioned as a visual spectacle with international ambitions, while *Pralay's* genre and scale could give Bollywood its first serious sci-fi blockbuster.

Vicky Kaushal doesn't do things halfway. He never has. The man spent months living in smoky interiors for *Sardar Udham* and bulked up beyond recognition for *Chhaava*. Now he's doing it again — and this time, the character he's becoming is literally, mythologically, immortal.
